Twofold’s gestures use Android’s Accessibility Service API. With your permission, Twofold uses it only to:

• open Android’s notifications and Quick Settings when you swipe down on Home
• run the actions you give a gesture or button: Home, Back, Recents, close notifications, Android’s app drawer, lock screen, screenshot, power menu, split screen and play/pause
• show the dock handle, the dock and Big Buttons over other apps, and open your dock apps from there, if you turn them on

Twofold can’t read what’s on your screen or what you type, doesn’t watch what you do in other apps, and collects and shares no data through this service. Nothing leaves your phone.

Tap Agree to open Accessibility settings, then turn on “Twofold gestures & overlays”.

If it’s greyed out, or Android says “Restricted setting”, tap App Info, open the ⋮ menu, choose “Allow restricted settings”, then come back and turn it on. Android asks this once for apps installed from outside an app store.

Twofold reads your notifications to show badges on app icons, an app’s recent notifications and media controls in its panel, and what’s playing. Notification content stays in memory on your phone only while it’s shown. It’s never saved, logged or sent anywhere.\n\nTap Agree to open Android’s settings, then allow Twofold.

Twofold reads which apps you opened and when, to suggest the apps you use most and to put a dot beside dock apps you used in the last hour. This stays on your phone and is never sent anywhere.\n\nTap Agree to open Android’s settings, then allow Twofold.
